svg.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Taking a Case
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-statutory-and-risk-routing; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Taking a Case; subtitle: Advance only with documented evidence; route failures explicitly.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Read sequentially: passing a check advances to the next check. The numeric field is a check ordinal, not a probability. Determine the applicable jurisdiction and current statutory text for each case; California and New York are concrete examples, not a nationwide substitute.; caption: Registration, contract timing, ownership, and secure handling must be resolved before a case enters paid delivery.; stages: label: Finder status and authority; value: Verify required registration and permitted representative activity; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Check the treasury's finder requirements and any applicable occupational licensing rules. If required credentials or owner authorization are absent, pause the engagement and identify the specific missing requirement.; label: Agreement timing and fee; value: Test statutory dates, fee limits, and contract terms; numeric value: 2.0; detail: For California, examine Code of Civil Procedure section 1582; for New York, Abandoned Property Law section 1416. Document relevant event dates and fee calculations. Route premature cases to a dated revisit list; reject prohibited fees.; label: Ownership and case value; value: Verify the claimant and calculate expected contribution; numeric value: 3.0; detail: California Code of Civil Procedure section 1540 anchors the claim process. Escalate conflicting identities or successor rights. Decline cases whose expected lawful fees cannot cover research, evidence, delivery, and collection costs.; label: Privacy and owner understanding; value: Protect identity evidence and disclose direct claiming; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Assess California Civil Code section 1798.81.5 where applicable. Use restricted encrypted storage, multifactor authentication, and expiring document links. Explain that the owner can claim directly; pause if understanding or secure evidence collection remains unresolved.
